framework_version: BMJ 2025;388:e082505 (Moons et al), evaluation branch subset

branch_meaning.term: Model evaluation: assesses risk of bias in the predictive performance estimates.
branch_meaning.not_to_be_confused_with: Model development, which assesses quality, not bias.
branch_meaning.modelaudit_scope: ModelAudit currently implements an eight-question subset of the model-evaluation branch only; it is not a complete PROBAST+AI assessment and cannot support official domain-level or overall judgements.

rules.text: All signalling questions are phrased so that yes or probably yes indicates low risk of bias.
Any no or probably no flags the potential for bias; assessors use judgement to rate the whole domain.
No information is used only when reported information is insufficient to permit a judgement.
Not applicable may be available for items not applicable to certain model types or situations.

standard.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, Table 2 footnote (p. 8) and p. 10

official_statements.text: For model evaluation, each domain is judged as low, high or unclear risk of bias, based on the signalling question answers and assessor judgement.
A no answer does not automatically result in a high risk of bias rating for the entire domain.
Step 4 combines the four domain ratings into an overall judgement (low, high or unclear). The detailed guidance is in supplementary table 3, which has not been extracted.

modelaudit_decisions.text: The system never proposes or computes a domain risk-of-bias judgement. It only summarises the answers and flags questions answered no or probably no for attention.

Because only a subset of each domain's questions is assessed (see domains.coverage), any domain judgement a reviewer records must be labelled as based on a subset and is not an official PROBAST+AI domain rating.
No overall (Step 4) risk-of-bias judgement and no numeric score are produced in the MVP.

domain_judgement.official_guidance_status: Official domain-level and overall judgement procedures have been reviewed in Supplementary Table 3. They are not applied to this eight-question subset because it does not cover all signalling questions in any domain.
domain_judgement.modelaudit_scope_warning: Do not generate or imply official PROBAST+AI domain-level or overall risk-of-bias judgements from this incomplete subset. Report question-level findings, evidence, uncertainty, and domain coverage counts with an explicit incomplete-coverage warning.

official.definition: Concern that the participants and setting, the predictors, or the outcome do not match the review question or the assessor's intended use of the model.
official.requires: A specified review question or intended use, defined with PICOTS in Step 1.
official.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, pp. 10-11 and Table 2, p. 8

modelaudit_decisions.text: Applicability stays not assessed unless the reviewer supplies the intended use or PICOTS. The transportability layer is deferred, so no automatic comparison is made.
Applicability judgements are never merged with risk-of-bias judgements, and are stored in a separate structure.

applicability_assessment.modelaudit_scope_warning: Applicability is separate from risk of bias and depends on the review question and intended use (PICOTS). Do not infer intended use from the paper alone. Leave applicability unassessed unless the reviewer supplies the relevant review context.

step2_classification.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, p. 10 (Step 2) and Box 1, pp. 3-4
official_notes: A separate assessment is done for each model and, as relevant, for each of the apparent, internal and external evaluation components (p. 9, p. 11).
For studies that only develop models, both parts of PROBAST+AI must usually still be completed (p. 11). The MVP assesses the evaluation part only.

questions.official_wording: Did the inclusions and exclusions of study participants result in a representative dataset?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain participants and data sources, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?

official_notes.text: The paper says data used to evaluate a model that are not representative of the assessor's target population can make performance estimates misleading, particularly in subgroups.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, Discussion, p. 12

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Eligibility criteria and exclusions applied to the evaluation dataset
Statements about who is missing from or over-represented in the evaluation data
The population the model is intended for, if stated
retrieval_queries: inclusion and exclusion criteria evaluation cohort
common_misinterpretations: Representative is relative to an intended population. If none is stated, answer no information, not no.
Exclusions for missing data belong here only if they changed who is in the evaluation dataset.

official_guidance.summary: Judge representativeness relative to the population relevant to the model's intended use; representativeness is contextual.
points: Review eligibility criteria, recruitment or sampling, inclusions, exclusions, and who is missing or over-represented.
Consider whether selection could distort performance estimates overall or in relevant subgroups, including disadvantaged or marginalised groups.

If the intended population or information needed to judge representativeness is not reported, do not infer that the dataset is representative or non-representative; use No information when the report is insufficient.
Distinguish exclusions that determine who enters the evaluation dataset from post-enrolment exclusions due to missing or censored data, which are considered under PE-4.3.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-1.3, p. 9

questions.official_wording: Were the predictors included in the model available at the time the model was intended to be used?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain predictors, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: When each predictor was measured
When the model is intended to be used in the care pathway
Any predictor measured after the point of intended use
retrieval_queries: predictors measured at admission or at follow-up
intended point of use of the model
common_misinterpretations: Needs the intended time of use. If the paper never states it, answer no information.
A predictor existing in the dataset does not show it would be available at the point of use.

official_guidance.summary: Assess whether every predictor used by the evaluated model would be available at the actual intended point of use in the care pathway.
points: Establish the intended prediction time or decision point, then compare it with when each predictor is measured or becomes available.

A predictor measured only after the intended prediction time may introduce bias or make the model unusable at that point; for example, an intraoperative or postoperative variable is unavailable for a genuinely preoperative prediction.
This is not asking whether all potentially useful predictors were collected or whether predictor values were missing. Missing predictor data and their handling belong to the Analysis domain.
A predictor being present in the research dataset does not establish that it would be available at the intended point of use.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-2.4, p. 11

questions.official_wording: Were outcomes defined and assessed appropriately?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain outcomes, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 3.1 Was the outcome determined appropriately? / 3.2 Was a pre-specified or standard outcome definition used? / 3.3 Were predictors excluded from the outcome definition?

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Outcome definition and reference standard
How and when the outcome was determined and by whom
Whether a standard or pre-specified definition was used
Any overlap between predictors and the outcome definition
retrieval_queries: predictors used to define the outcome
common_misinterpretations: Naming the outcome is not showing it was defined and assessed appropriately.
Appropriateness is a judgement. If the paper gives too little detail, answer no information.

official_guidance.summary: Assess whether the outcome was defined and measured using a suitable and sufficiently consistent reference.
points: Consider the outcome definition, measurement method, timing, assessor, and reference standard, including measurement error or misclassification.

Consider whether a standard or prespecified definition was used. Non-standard definitions, data-driven thresholds, or thresholds selected after examining the data can make outcome classification less reliable or introduce bias.
For composite outcomes, examine whether components are clearly defined and whether combining them is appropriate; components may differ in importance or ascertainment.
Consider whether routine-care records, registries, or other data sources may apply inconsistent definitions or less reliable ascertainment.
Merely naming the outcome does not show that it was defined and assessed appropriately. If detail is insufficient to judge, use No information.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-3.1, pp. 5 and 12

questions.official_wording: Was model evaluation based on only apparent performance avoided?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain analyses, p. 8

components.multiple_components: Assess each component separately; do not collapse apparent, internal, and external evaluations.
components.unclear_component: Do not infer the component; use no_information or request reviewer clarification.

conditional_rule.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, PE-4.1, p. 14; Supplementary Table 3

official_notes.text: Apparent performance means performance estimated on the same data used for development. Evaluation can be apparent, internal validation or external validation.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, Box 1, p. 3 and p. 9

official_notes.text: A separate assessment is done for each model and, as relevant, for each of the apparent, internal and external evaluation components.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, p. 9 and p. 11

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: How performance was estimated: same data, splitting, resampling or cross-validation, or separate participants
Whether any evaluation used data not used for development
retrieval_queries: performance on a held-out test set
common_misinterpretations: Yes means only-apparent evaluation was avoided. A held-out split or external data both count as not apparent-only; the type of evaluation is recorded separately in the assessment context.

official_guidance.summary: Identify the evaluation component and assess whether evaluation based only on development data (apparent performance) was avoided.
points: Apparent performance is estimated using the same participants/data used to develop the model and is generally optimistic.

Internal validation estimates performance using the development dataset with a validation procedure such as resampling or a training/test split. External validation uses participant data independent of development data and internal validation.
Assess each reported component separately: apparent, internal validation, and external validation are not interchangeable.

If the only reported evaluation is apparent performance, the answer to PE-4.1 is No. Subsequent questions specific to internal and external validation are not relevant to that apparent-only component and must not be forced into Yes/No answers.
If multiple components are reported, retain separate component-level assessments rather than collapsing them into one answer.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-4.1, p. 14; Supplementary Table 3

questions.official_wording: Was there evidence that the sample size was reasonable?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain analyses, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 4.1 Were there a reasonable number of participants with the outcome?

official_notes.text: Bias must not be confused with imprecision. Imprecision means wide confidence intervals from a small evaluation sample.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, p. 9 and Box 1, p. 3

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Number of participants and outcome events in the evaluation data
Any sample size calculation or justification for evaluation
Confidence interval widths as a sign of imprecision
retrieval_queries: number of participants and outcome events in the test set
common_misinterpretations: Do not apply a numeric rule of thumb. Decide only on the evidence the paper gives, and use no information if there is none.
Development sample size is not evaluation sample size.

official_guidance.summary: Assess whether the evaluation sample size was reasonable. Distinguish systematic bias from statistical imprecision.
points: Consider the number of participants and outcome events in the evaluation sample, the distribution of predicted risks, performance measures, and relevant subgroup analyses.
Consider whether a sample-size justification or other evidence supports the adequacy of the evaluation sample.
Small samples can produce imprecise estimates and wide confidence intervals. Imprecision is not itself the same as risk of bias, although it affects confidence in the performance estimate.
Do not apply simplistic rules of thumb (such as a fixed minimum event count) as automatic pass/fail thresholds; adequacy depends on the evaluation context and required precision.
Do not substitute development sample size for the size of the dataset used to evaluate performance.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-4.2, p. 14

questions.official_wording: Were participants with missing or censored data handled appropriately in the analysis?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain analyses, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 4.4 Were participants with missing data handled appropriately?

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Amount of missing or censored data
How missing or censored data were handled in the evaluation analysis
Exclusions made because of missing data
retrieval_queries: missing data handling imputation complete case
participants excluded because of missing values
common_misinterpretations: Reporting that data were missing is not the same as saying how they were handled.
If the paper states there were no missing data, record that as the evidence.

official_guidance.summary: Assess whether missing or censored observations and exclusions due to them were handled appropriately in performance evaluation.
points: Identify the amount and pattern of missingness or censoring, affected variables, and the number and characteristics of participants excluded from analysis.
Consider whether complete-case analysis or other exclusions could selectively remove participants and distort the evaluation sample or performance estimates.
Consider the plausibility of the missingness mechanism, including missing not at random. No universal missing-data percentage automatically determines acceptability.
Consider whether the selected approach (for example, imputation or an intended-use missing-data strategy) was appropriate and implemented without information leakage.
For time-to-event outcomes, consider censoring and competing risks where relevant.
A statement that data were missing is not enough to establish appropriate handling. An explicit report of no missing data is relevant evidence.
If the report does not provide enough information to judge handling, use No information rather than assuming it was appropriate.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-4.3, p. 15

questions.official_wording: If data splitting was done to create training and test datasets, was there evidence that data leakage was avoided?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain analyses, p. 8

conditional_rule.uncertain_design: Do not automatically assign not_applicable if the evaluation component or split design is unclear; use no_information or flag for reviewer clarification.
conditional_rule.machine_checkable: Partially; requires reviewer-verified evaluation-component and split-design classification.

official_notes.text: Data leakage means data from the development phase inadvertently included during evaluation, typically giving over-optimistic performance.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, Box 1, p. 3

official_notes.text: The not applicable category may be available for items that do not apply to certain types of model or situation.

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Whether the data were split into training and test sets
How the split was done, including at participant level
Steps showing development choices did not use the test data
retrieval_queries: data were split into training and test sets
participants in both training and test data
preprocessing or feature selection performed before splitting
common_misinterpretations: If no splitting was done, the official answer option is not applicable, not no.
Absence of evidence of leakage is no information, not no.

official_guidance.summary: This question concerns data leakage when a training/test split was used. Applicability depends on the evaluation component and actual validation design.
points: Data leakage occurs when information from evaluation/test data influences development or evaluation procedures in a way that can make performance estimates optimistic.

Examples include participants or records appearing across training and test sets, or preprocessing, feature selection, or other data-dependent development decisions being performed on the full dataset before splitting.
For internal validation using a training/test split, assess whether the split and subsequent workflow prevented leakage.

For internal validation using resampling without a training/test split, this split-specific question is not applicable; PE-4.6 (omitted from this subset) addresses repetition of development steps within resampling.
For apparent performance and external validation, PE-4.5 is not applicable according to the E&E guidance.

If the report does not establish the evaluation component or whether an internal training/test split was used, do not automatically assign Not applicable. Use No information or flag for reviewer clarification.
Absence of a reported leakage event is not evidence that leakage was avoided; examine the split and timing of preprocessing and development decisions.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-4.5, p. 15

questions.official_wording: Was the predictive performance of the model evaluated appropriately—for example, calibration, discrimination, and net benefit?

wording_source.location: Table 2, model evaluation, domain analyses, p. 8

lineage.probast_2019: 4.7 Were relevant model performance measures evaluated appropriately?

official_notes.text: Model evaluation estimates performance for example by Brier score, discrimination, calibration and clinical usefulness such as decision curve analysis.
official_notes.source: Moons et al, BMJ 2025;388:e082505, Box 1, p. 4

questions.official_guidance_status: Reviewed and summarized from PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4 (Explanation and Elaboration Light); see official_guidance.source.

modelaudit.origin: ModelAudit operational content. Not official PROBAST+AI text.
evidence_focus: Which performance measures were reported
Whether calibration and discrimination were both assessed
Whether clinical usefulness (net benefit) was assessed
common_misinterpretations: The examples in the question are examples, not a fixed list. Do not answer no only because net benefit is absent; record exactly which measures were found.
This is distinct from TRIPOD+AI item 12e, which concerns whether measures are specified in the Methods.

official_guidance.summary: Assess whether predictive performance was evaluated with appropriate measures and methods. Calibration and discrimination are complementary; net benefit/clinical usefulness is also relevant where appropriate.
points: Consider calibration (agreement between predicted and observed risks) and discrimination (ability to distinguish participants with and without the outcome). Both should be assessed using appropriate methods.
Calibration plots are generally more informative than relying only on a goodness-of-fit test; assess the method, not merely whether a statistic is named.
Consider clinical usefulness or net benefit where relevant, for example decision-curve analysis and thresholds tied to the intended decision.

Do not automatically answer No solely because net benefit is absent; record which measures were assessed and judge appropriateness in context. Absence of calibration or discrimination is more consequential.
Consider whether threshold-based classification discarded useful information or thresholds were selected in a data-driven manner.
Consider performance in relevant subgroups where reported or needed to identify important differences or inequities.
Do not confuse this with reporting transparency about whether measures were prespecified in Methods; this question concerns the appropriateness of the performance evaluation.
official_guidance.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 4, Explanation and Elaboration Light, PE-4.7, p. 16

modelaudit_global_rules: Use only the supplied excerpts. Every answer other than no_information needs at least one verbatim quotation with chunk_id and PDF page.
no_information and not_assessed are different. not_assessed means the system did not run the question. no_information is an official answer meaning the paper gave too little to judge.
A quotation that exists in the paper does not by itself show that it supports the answer.
Never state or imply that a model is clinically valid, safe or ready for use.
Do not use TRIPOD+AI reporting categories. PROBAST+AI answers use the official response scale only.

modelaudit_global_rules.origin: ModelAudit engineering safeguard; not an official PROBAST+AI rule.
modelaudit_global_rules.rule: A quotation is required for an assessed answer under the current MVP evidence policy, but quotation presence or lexical matching is not sufficient to justify the answer.
requirements: Explain how the quoted passage supports or contradicts the signalling question.
Interpret the passage in context; do not rely on isolated keyword matches.
Distinguish direct evidence, reasonable interpretation, absence of reported information, and reviewer-dependent judgement.
A passage that merely mentions a topic is not proof that the relevant method was performed appropriately.
If retrieved evidence is ambiguous, incomplete, or insufficient, use No information or refer the finding for human review.
Quote existence in the PDF is a source-integrity check, not semantic verification.

modelaudit_global_rules.origin: ModelAudit engineering safeguard; not an official PROBAST+AI rule.
modelaudit_global_rules.rule: Keep official framework content separate from ModelAudit operational choices.
requirements: Identify official wording, response options, applicability guidance, and E&E summaries as PROBAST+AI source content.
Label retrieval queries, evidence-focus lists, quote requirements, automated routing, and product limitations as ModelAudit operational content.
Never describe this eight-question subset as the complete PROBAST+AI tool.

omitted_questions.official_wording: If class imbalance correction was used during model development, was the evaluation done in data without imbalance correction?
omitted_questions.coverage_implication: The subset does not assess whether evaluation data retained the natural outcome distribution after class-imbalance correction during development.
omitted_questions.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 3 and Supplementary Table 4, PE-4.4, p. 15

omitted_questions.official_wording: If resampling was done, were all steps in the development process appropriately repeated?
omitted_questions.coverage_implication: The subset does not assess whether all development steps (such as imputation, variable selection, hyperparameter tuning, and model fitting) were repeated within each resample. This is a material limitation for resampling-based internal validation.
omitted_questions.source: PROBAST+AI Supplementary Table 3 and Supplementary Table 4, PE-4.6, p. 16
